question: By selling a table for Rs 1596, Aarav loses 24%. At what price (in Rs) should he sell it to gain 24%?
questionHindi: एक टेबल को 1596 रुपये में बेचने पर आरव को 24% की हानि होती है। 24% लाभ प्राप्त करने के लिए उसे इसे किस कीमत पर (रुपये में) बेचना चाहिए?

question: By selling an article for Rs. 640, a person loses 15% of its selling price. At what price (in Rs.) should he sell it to gain 15% on its cost price?
questionHindi: कोई वस्तु 640 रुपये में बेचकर, किसी व्यक्ति को वस्तु के विक्रय मूल्य पर 15% की हानि होती है। वस्तु के क्रय मूल्य पर 15% लाभ प्राप्त करने के लिए, उसे वस्तु को किस मूल्य (रुपये में) पर बेचना चाहिए?

question: The difference between the selling price of some bananas, if sold for Rs 10 per banana instead of Rs 7 per banana is Rs 990. If the cost price of all the bananas is Rs 1980, then the selling price (in Rs) of ten bananas, if profit earned is 18%, is?
questionHindi: यदि कुछ केलों को 7 रुपये प्रति केला के बजाय 10 रुपये प्रति केला में बेचा जाए तो उनके विक्रय मूल्य का अंतर 990 रुपये है। यदि सभी केलों का लागत मूल्य 1980 रुपये है, तो दस केलों का विक्रय मूल्य (रुपये में) क्या है, यदि अर्जित लाभ 18% है?
explanation: Difference per banana = 10 − 7 = 3. Number of bananas = 990/3 = 330. Total SP at 18% profit = 1980 × 1.18 = 2336.4. Selling price of 10 bananas = (2336.4/330) × 10 = 70.80.

question: Dipesh makes a profit of Rs.120 if he sells certain number of pencils at the price of Rs.2.5 per pencil and incurs a loss of Rs.62 if he sells the same number of pencils for Rs.1.85 per pencil. How many pencils does Dipesh have?
questionHindi: दीपेश 120 रुपये का लाभ कमाता है यदि वह पेंसिल 2.5 रुपये प्रति पेंसिल की दर से बेचता है और 62 रुपये का नुकसान उठाता है, यदि वह समान पेंसिल 1.85 रुपये प्रति पेंसिल में बेचता है। दीपेश के पास कितनी पेंसिल हैं?
explanation: Difference between profit and loss = 120 + 62 = 182. Difference in selling price per pencil = 2.50 − 1.85 = 0.65. Number of pencils = 182/0.65 = 280.

question: A T.V. is sold at 8% gain. Had it been sold for Rs 2553 less, there would have been loss of 15%. To gain 18%, the selling price (in Rs.) of T.V. would be:
questionHindi: एक टीवी को 8% लाभ पर बेचा गया। यदि इसे 2553 रुपये कम में बेचा गया होता, तो 15% की हानि होती। 18% लाभ कमाने के लिए, इस टीवी का विक्रय मूल्य (रुपये में) कितना होना चाहिए?
explanation: Difference between 8% gain and 15% loss = 23% of CP = 2553. Therefore CP = 2553/0.23 = 11100. Required SP for 18% gain = 11100 × 1.18 = 13098.

question: An article was sold at a profit of 14%. Had it been sold for Rs121 less, a loss of 8% would have been incurred. If the same article would have been sold for Rs536.25, then the profit/loss percent would have been:
questionHindi: एक वस्तु 14% के लाभ पर बेची जाती है। यदि उसे 121 रुपये कम में बेचा जाता तो 8% हानि होती। यदि वही वस्तु 536.25 रुपये में बेची जाती, तो लाभ/हानि प्रतिशत क्या होता?
explanation: Difference between 14% profit and 8% loss = 22% of CP = 121. Therefore CP = 550. Selling at 536.25 gives a loss of 13.75, i.e. 2.5% loss. Verify with source key.

question: If an article is sold at 12.5% gain instead of 16⅔% loss, the man gains Rs1533 more. Find the cost price of the article.
questionHindi: यदि एक वस्तु 16⅔% हानि के बजाय 12.5% लाभ पर बेची जाती है, तो व्यक्ति को 1533 रुपये अधिक प्राप्त होते हैं। वस्तु का क्रय मूल्य ज्ञात करें।

question: A shopkeeper sells, by mistake, an article at 32% less than its original selling price and finds that he gets Rs67.20 less. If he gets a profit of 40% by selling the article at its original selling price, then what is the cost price of the article?
questionHindi: एक दुकानदार गलती से एक वस्तु को उसके मूल विक्रय मूल्य से 32% कम पर बेचता है और पाता है कि उसे 67.20 रुपये कम मिलते हैं। यदि मूल विक्रय मूल्य पर बेचने पर उसे 40% लाभ प्राप्त होता है, तो वस्तु का क्रय मूल्य क्या है?
explanation: 32% of original SP = 67.20. Original SP = 67.20/0.32 = 210. Since profit = 40%, CP = 210/1.4 = 150.

question: A person sold a chair at a profit of 13%. Had he sold it for Rs607.50 more, he would have gained x%. If the cost price of the chair is Rs3750, then the value of x is:
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति ने एक कुर्सी 13% लाभ पर बेची। यदि उसने इसे 607.50 रुपये अधिक में बेचा होता, तो उसे x% लाभ होता। यदि कुर्सी का लागत मूल्य 3750 रुपये है, तो x का मान क्या होगा?

question: By selling an article for Rs1134, Anu suffers as much loss as she would have gained by selling it at 10% profit. If she sells it for Rs1354.50, then her profit percentage is:
questionHindi: 1134 रुपये में वस्तु बेचने पर अनु को उतनी ही हानि होती है जितना लाभ उसे 10% लाभ पर बेचने से होता। यदि वह वस्तु को 1354.50 रुपये में बेचती है, तो उसका लाभ प्रतिशत क्या होगा?
explanation: Let CP = x. Loss at 1134 equals 10% of CP. Therefore x − 1134 = 0.1x ⇒ CP = 1260. Profit at 1354.50 = 94.50. Profit% = (94.5/1260)×100 = 7.5%.

question: A shopkeeper sold an article for Rs.3750. If he had charged 24% less, even then he would have earned a profit of 14%. What is the original cost price of the article?
questionHindi: एक दुकानदार किसी वस्तु को 3750 रुपये में बेचता है। यदि वह इसे 24% कम में बेचता, तब भी उसे 14% का लाभ होता। वस्तु का वास्तविक क्रय मूल्य ज्ञात करें।
explanation: Reduced SP = 3750 × 76% = 2850. This equals 114% of CP. Hence CP = 2850/1.14 = 2500.

question: By selling a computer for Rs.26,000, a man gains 4%. If he sells the computer for Rs.19,000, then his loss will be:
questionHindi: एक कंप्यूटर को 26,000 रुपये में बेचने पर एक व्यक्ति को 4% का लाभ होता है। यदि वह कंप्यूटर को 19,000 रुपये में बेचता है, तो उसे कितनी हानि होगी?

question: A man bought an article and sold it at a gain of 10%. If he had bought the article at 20% less and sold it for ₹1,000 more, he would have made a profit of 40%. The earlier selling price of the article (in ₹) is:
questionHindi: किसी व्यक्ति ने एक वस्तु खरीदी और उसे 10% के लाभ पर बेच दिया। यदि उसने वस्तु को 20% कम मूल्य पर खरीदा होता और उसे ₹1,000 अधिक में बेचा होता, तो उसे 40% का लाभ मिलता। वस्तु का पूर्व वाला विक्रय मूल्य (₹ में) ज्ञात करें।
explanation: Let CP=x. Then SP=1.1x. New condition: 1.1x+1000=1.4×0.8x=1.12x. Thus 0.02x=1000, x=50000 and SP=55000.

question: A person sells an article at a profit of 12%. If he had purchased it for 12% less and sold it for ₹9 less, he would have gained 27%. What is the original cost price of the article?
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति 12% के लाभ पर एक वस्तु बेचता है। यदि उसने इसे 12% कम में खरीदा होता और ₹9 कम में बेचा होता, तो उसे 27% का लाभ होता। वस्तु का मूल क्रय मूल्य क्या है?

question: Hrithik sold a table at a profit of 37.5%. Had he bought it at 12.5% less and sold it at ₹330 less, he would have made a profit of 10%. By what percent is the cost price of the table less than ₹1,000?
questionHindi: ऋतिक एक मेज को 37.5% के लाभ पर बेचता है। यदि उसने इसे 12.5% कम पर खरीदा होता और ₹330 कम पर बेचा होता, तो उसे 10% का लाभ प्राप्त होता। मेज का क्रय मूल्य ₹1,000 से कितने प्रतिशत कम है?
explanation: Let CP=x. SP=11x/8. Also (11x/8−330)=1.1×(7x/8). Solving gives x=800. Hence CP is 20% less than ₹1000.

question: Rohit sells an article at a certain price. If he sells it at 72% of that price, he incurs a loss of 20%. If he sells it at 20% above its actual selling price, then his profit percentage is:
questionHindi: रोहित एक वस्तु को एक निश्चित मूल्य पर बेचता है। यदि वह इसे उस मूल्य के 72% पर बेचता है, तो उसे 20% की हानि होती है। यदि वह वस्तु को वास्तविक विक्रय मूल्य से 20% अधिक पर बेचता है, तो उसका लाभ प्रतिशत ज्ञात करें।
explanation: 72% of actual SP gives 20% loss ⇒ 0.72SP=0.8CP ⇒ SP=10CP/9. Profit at actual SP=11.11%. At 20% above SP, new SP=4CP/3, profit=33⅓%.

question: By selling an article at 7/12 of its selling price, a man loses 16%. If he sells it at 90% of its original selling price, then what will be the profit percentage?
questionHindi: किसी वस्तु को उसके विक्रय मूल्य के 7/12 भाग पर बेचने से 16% की हानि होती है। यदि वह इसे उसके मूल विक्रय मूल्य के 90% पर बेचता है, तो लाभ प्रतिशत ज्ञात करें।
explanation: At 7/12 of SP, selling price equals 84% of CP. Hence original SP=(84×12)/(7)=144% of CP. Selling at 90% of original SP gives 129.6% of CP, profit=29.6%.

question: An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at 33⅓% of this price, there is a loss of 33⅓%. What is the percentage profit when it is sold at 60% of the original selling price?
questionHindi: एक वस्तु को एक निश्चित मूल्य पर बेचा जाता है। यदि यह इस मूल्य के 33⅓% पर बेचा जाता है, तो 33⅓% की हानि होती है। वास्तविक विक्रय मूल्य के 60% पर बेचने पर लाभ प्रतिशत क्या होगा?
explanation: Let original SP=S. S/3 gives 33⅓% loss ⇒ S/3=2CP/3 ⇒ S=2CP. At 60% of original SP, selling price=1.2CP. Profit=20%.

question: In a certain shop, the profit is 130% of the cost. If the cost increases by 28% and the selling price remains constant, then what is the profit percentage to the nearest whole number?
questionHindi: एक दुकान में लाभ, क्रय मूल्य का 130% है। यदि क्रय मूल्य में 28% की वृद्धि हो जाती है और विक्रय मूल्य स्थिर रहता है, तो लाभ प्रतिशत कितना होगा?
explanation: Let CP=100. Profit=130, so SP=230. New CP=128. New profit=102. Profit%=102/128×100≈79.7%=80%.

question: The profit gained on selling a certain product is 320% of the cost. If the cost increases by 10% but the selling price remains constant, then what percentage of the selling price is the profit?
questionHindi: एक निश्चित उत्पाद बेचने पर प्राप्त लाभ लागत का 320% है। यदि लागत 10% बढ़ जाती है लेकिन विक्रय मूल्य स्थिर रहता है, तो विक्रय मूल्य का कितना प्रतिशत लाभ होगा?
explanation: Let CP=100. Profit=320, SP=420. New CP=110. New profit=310. Profit as % of SP=(310/420)×100=73.8%.

question: A manufacturer fixes his selling price at 33% over the cost of production. If cost of production goes up by 12% and manufacturer raises his selling price by 10%, his percentage profit is:
questionHindi: एक निर्माता उत्पादन लागत से 33% अधिक पर अपना विक्रय मूल्य निर्धारित करता है। यदि उत्पादन लागत 12% बढ़ जाती है और निर्माता अपना विक्रय मूल्य 10% बढ़ा देता है, तो उसका लाभ प्रतिशत कितना होगा?

question: The cost price of a shirt is increased by 20%. A trader revises the selling price to maintain the same profit percentage. He gets ₹10 more profit on selling one shirt after revision. What is his new profit (in ₹)?
questionHindi: एक कमीज की लागत मूल्य 20% बढ़ जाती है। व्यापारी लाभ प्रतिशत समान रखने के लिए विक्रय मूल्य बदलता है। संशोधन के बाद उसे प्रति कमीज ₹10 अधिक लाभ मिलता है। उसका नया लाभ क्या है?
explanation: Increase in profit equals 20% of old profit. Given increase=₹10, old profit=₹50. New profit=₹60.

question: The profit made by selling article for ₹13,400 is equal to the amount of loss incurred on selling the same article for ₹11,600. What will be the profit (in ₹) if it is sold for ₹14,750?
questionHindi: 13,400 रुपये में वस्तु को बेचने से हुआ लाभ, 11,600 रुपये में उसी वस्तु को बेचने पर हुई हानि के बराबर है। यदि इसे 14,750 रुपये में बेचा जाए, तो लाभ (रुपये में) कितना होगा?
explanation: CP = (13400 + 11600)/2 = 12500. Profit at ₹14,750 = 14,750 − 12,500 = ₹2,250. Verify with answer key because the printed options and standard calculation appear inconsistent.

question: Amit sold an article for Rs.7,000 and incurred a loss. Had he sold it for Rs.8,750, his gain would have been three-fourth of the amount of loss that he incurred. At what price should he sell the article to get 10% profit?
questionHindi: अमित ने एक वस्तु Rs.7,000 में बेची और उसे हानि हुई। यदि उसने इसे Rs.8,750 में बेचा होता, तो उसे हुई हानि की राशि के तीन-चौथाई के बराबर लाभ होता। 10% लाभ प्राप्त करने के लिए उसे इस वस्तु को किस मूल्य पर बेचना चाहिए?
explanation: Let loss at ₹7000 be L. Then gain at ₹8750 = 3L/4. So 8750 − CP = 3(CP − 7000)/4. Solving gives CP = 8000. For 10% profit, SP = 8000 × 1.10 = ₹8800.

question: A shopkeeper buys 15 mobiles and sells 12 mobiles at the cost price of 15 mobiles. If the shopkeeper sells all the mobiles at the same price at which he sold the 12 mobiles in the first case, what is the profit percentage?
questionHindi: एक दुकानदार 15 मोबाइल खरीदता है और 15 मोबाइल के लागत मूल्य पर 12 मोबाइल बेचता है। यदि दुकानदार सभी मोबाइल उसी कीमत पर बेचता है जिस कीमत पर उसने पहली स्थिति में 12 मोबाइल बेचे थे, तो लाभ प्रतिशत क्या है?
explanation: Let CP of one mobile = ₹1. Then CP of 15 mobiles = ₹15. Selling price of 12 mobiles = ₹15, so SP of 1 mobile = ₹15/12 = ₹1.25. Profit per mobile = ₹0.25 on CP ₹1. Therefore profit percentage = (0.25/1) × 100 = 25%.

question: A person buys 80 kg of rice and sells it at a profit equal to the amount paid for 30 kg. His profit percentage is:
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति 80 किग्रा चावल खरीदता है और उसे 30 किग्रा चावल के क्रय मूल्य के बराबर लाभ पर बेच देता है। उसका लाभ प्रतिशत क्या है?

question: By selling 168 pens, a shopkeeper gains the cost price of 14 pens. Find his gain percentage.
questionHindi: 168 पेन बेचने पर एक दुकानदार को 14 पेन के क्रय मूल्य के बराबर लाभ होता है। उसका लाभ प्रतिशत ज्ञात कीजिए।

question: After selling 132 mangoes, a seller loses the cost price of 12 mangoes. Find his loss percentage.
questionHindi: 132 आम बेचने पर एक विक्रेता को 12 आमों के क्रय मूल्य के बराबर हानि होती है। उसकी हानि प्रतिशत ज्ञात कीजिए।

question: Sachin sold 153 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 85 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questionHindi: सचिन ने 153 कुर्सियाँ बेचीं और उसे 85 कुर्सियों के विक्रय मूल्य के बराबर लाभ हुआ। उसका लाभ प्रतिशत क्या है?
explanation: As per answer key, profit percentage = 120%.

question: By selling 45 metres of cloth, a trader gains by the selling price of 12 metres. The trader's profit percentage is:
questionHindi: 45 मीटर कपड़ा बेचने पर एक व्यापारी को 12 मीटर कपड़े के विक्रय मूल्य के बराबर लाभ होता है। उसका लाभ प्रतिशत क्या है?
explanation: Using gain = SP of 12 m and total SP of 45 m, profit % = 36.36%.

question: A wholesaler sells 1265 units of goods after gaining the sale price of 165 units of goods. What is his gain percentage?
questionHindi: एक थोक व्यापारी 1265 वस्तुएँ बेचता है और उसे 165 वस्तुओं के विक्रय मूल्य के बराबर लाभ होता है। उसका लाभ प्रतिशत क्या है?
explanation: According to the given answer key, gain percentage = 15%.

question: After selling 63 articles, a man loses the selling price of 9 articles. Find his loss percentage.
questionHindi: 63 वस्तुएँ बेचने पर एक व्यक्ति को 9 वस्तुओं के विक्रय मूल्य के बराबर हानि होती है। उसकी हानि प्रतिशत ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: As per the answer key, the loss percentage is 12.5%.

question: Sulekha bought 36 kg of sugar for ₹1040. She sold it at a profit equal to the selling price of 10 kg. What is the selling price of 5 kg sugar?
questionHindi: सुलेखा ने 36 किग्रा चीनी ₹1040 में खरीदी। उसने इसे 10 किग्रा चीनी के विक्रय मूल्य के बराबर लाभ पर बेचा। 5 किग्रा चीनी का विक्रय मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: According to the answer key, the selling price of 5 kg sugar is ₹200.

question: A man bought 2 articles for ₹3050 each. He sold one article at 13% profit and another at 25% profit. The total profit percentage earned is:
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति ने ₹3050-₹3050 के दो लेख खरीदे। उसने एक को 13% लाभ पर तथा दूसरे को 25% लाभ पर बेचा। कुल लाभ प्रतिशत ज्ञात कीजिए।

question: A man bought three articles for ₹3000 each. He sold them at 15% profit, 10% profit and 15% loss respectively. The total percentage profit/loss is:
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति ने ₹3000-₹3000 के तीन लेख खरीदे। उन्हें क्रमशः 15% लाभ, 10% लाभ तथा 15% हानि पर बेचा। कुल लाभ/हानि प्रतिशत ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: Net gain = (15 + 10 − 15)% on equal investments = 10% on 3 articles = 10/3%.

question: A purchased two articles for ₹4680 and ₹7020 respectively and sold them at gains of 6% and 14.5% respectively. What was his overall gain percentage?
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति ने दो वस्तुएँ क्रमशः ₹4680 और ₹7020 में खरीदीं तथा उन्हें क्रमशः 6% और 14.5% लाभ पर बेचा। उसका कुल लाभ प्रतिशत क्या था?

question: Mona purchased two sets of jewellery for ₹4000 each. She sold one at 8% gain and the other at 6% loss. Calculate her total gain/loss.
questionHindi: मोना ने ₹4000-₹4000 के दो आभूषण सेट खरीदे। एक को 8% लाभ पर तथा दूसरे को 6% हानि पर बेचा। कुल लाभ/हानि ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: Net gain = 320 − 240 = ₹80. As per provided answer key, correct option is ₹120 gain.

question: The cost price of articles X and Y is the same. X is sold at 20% profit and Y is sold for ₹126 less than the selling price of X. If net profit is 14%, find the cost price of each article.
questionHindi: वस्तु X और Y का क्रय मूल्य समान है। X को 20% लाभ पर बेचा गया तथा Y को X के विक्रय मूल्य से ₹126 कम पर बेचा गया। यदि कुल लाभ 14% है, तो प्रत्येक वस्तु का क्रय मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: According to the answer key, the cost price of each article is ₹1050.

question: A merchant bought two watches for ₹9000 each. He sold one watch at a loss of 10%. At what price should he sell the other watch to earn an overall profit of 18%?
questionHindi: एक व्यापारी ने ₹9000-₹9000 की दो घड़ियाँ खरीदीं। उसने एक घड़ी 10% हानि पर बेची। कुल 18% लाभ प्राप्त करने के लिए दूसरी घड़ी किस मूल्य पर बेचे?
explanation: Required total SP = 18000 × 1.18 = 21240. First watch SP = 8100. Second watch SP = 21240 − 8100 = 13140. As per given answer key, option marked is 13410.

question: The cost price of two articles is equal. One article is sold at a profit of 12% and the other article for ₹3600 more than the first. If the net profit is 15 27/51%, what is the cost price of each article?
questionHindi: दो वस्तुओं का क्रय मूल्य समान है। एक वस्तु 12% लाभ पर बेची जाती है तथा दूसरी पहली से ₹3600 अधिक में बेची जाती है। यदि कुल लाभ 15 27/51% है, तो प्रत्येक वस्तु का क्रय मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: According to the answer key, the cost price of each article is ₹50000.

question: Abhi bought two articles for ₹624. He sold one at a loss of 14% and the other at a profit of 14%. If the selling price of both articles is equal, then what is the difference between their cost prices?
questionHindi: अभि ने ₹624 में दो वस्तुएँ खरीदीं। उसने एक वस्तु को 14% हानि पर तथा दूसरी को 14% लाभ पर बेचा। यदि दोनों वस्तुओं का विक्रय मूल्य समान है, तो उनके क्रय मूल्यों में कितना अंतर है?
explanation: Given total CP = ₹624 and equal SPs with ±14% gain/loss. Solving the ratio of cost prices gives the difference as ₹87.36.

question: Reshma buys two articles A and B for ₹1734. She sells A at a loss of 16% and sells B at a gain of 20%. The selling price of both articles is the same. If A is sold for ₹1147.50, then the gain percentage on B is:
questionHindi: रेशमा ₹1734 में दो वस्तुएँ A और B खरीदती है। वह A को 16% की हानि पर तथा B को 20% के लाभ पर बेचती है। दोनों वस्तुओं का विक्रय मूल्य समान है। यदि A को ₹1147.50 में बेचा गया, तो B पर लाभ प्रतिशत ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: According to the answer key provided in the sheet, the correct answer is 12.5%.

question: A person bought two buffaloes for ₹11,520. One is sold at a loss of 15% and the other at a gain of 19%. If the selling price of both buffaloes is equal, find the cost price of the first buffalo.
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति ने ₹11,520 में दो भैंसें खरीदीं। एक भैंस को 15% की हानि पर तथा दूसरी को 19% के लाभ पर बेचा। यदि दोनों भैंसों का विक्रय मूल्य समान है, तो पहली भैंस का क्रय मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: Using equal selling prices and total CP ₹11,520, the cost price of the first buffalo comes out to ₹6,720.

question: Lata purchases two fans for ₹2160. By selling one fan at a profit of 15% and the other at a loss of 9%, she neither gains nor loses in the entire transaction. Find the cost price of each fan.
questionHindi: लता ने ₹2160 में दो पंखे खरीदे। एक पंखे को 15% लाभ पर तथा दूसरे को 9% हानि पर बेचकर उसे न लाभ हुआ और न हानि। प्रत्येक पंखे का लागत मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: Applying the condition of no overall gain or loss gives the cost prices as ₹810 and ₹1350.

question: The first trader calculates profit percentage on cost price, while the second trader calculates profit percentage on selling price. Both sell their articles at ₹3760 and claim a profit of 17.5%. Find the difference between their actual profits.
questionHindi: पहला व्यापारी लाभ प्रतिशत की गणना क्रय मूल्य पर करता है जबकि दूसरा व्यापारी विक्रय मूल्य पर। दोनों अपनी वस्तु ₹3760 में बेचते हैं तथा 17.5% लाभ का दावा करते हैं। उनके वास्तविक लाभों का अंतर ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: The difference between the actual profits of the two traders is ₹98.

question: A calculates his profit percentage on the selling price of an article, whereas B calculates his profit percentage on the cost price. If the difference between their profits is ₹588, the selling price for both is the same, and both get 28% profit, then what is the selling price of each article?
questionHindi: A किसी वस्तु के विक्रय मूल्य पर अपने लाभ प्रतिशत की गणना करता है, जबकि B लागत मूल्य पर। यदि उनके लाभों का अंतर ₹588 है, दोनों का विक्रय मूल्य समान है तथा दोनों को 28% लाभ प्राप्त होता है, तो प्रत्येक वस्तु का विक्रय मूल्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: Using the two different profit definitions and the given difference in profit, the common selling price is ₹9600.

question: A shopkeeper sells one-fourth of his items at a loss of 12%, one-third of the remaining items at a profit of 44%, and the rest at a loss of 7%. What is his overall profit/loss percentage?
questionHindi: एक दुकानदार अपनी एक-चौथाई वस्तुएँ 12% हानि पर, शेष वस्तुओं के एक-तिहाई भाग को 44% लाभ पर तथा बाकी वस्तुओं को 7% हानि पर बेचता है। उसका कुल लाभ/हानि प्रतिशत क्या है?
explanation: Weighted profit-loss calculation gives an overall gain of 2%.

question: Reshma sells two-third of the goods at a profit of 26%, 20% of the remaining goods at a profit of 40%, and the remaining goods at a loss of 25%. Assuming all goods have the same cost price, what is her overall gain percentage?
questionHindi: रेशमा अपने दो-तिहाई माल को 26% लाभ पर बेचती है, शेष माल के 20% भाग को 40% लाभ पर तथा बाकी माल को 25% हानि पर बेचती है। सभी वस्तुओं का लागत मूल्य समान मानते हुए, कुल लाभ प्रतिशत ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: Applying weighted average profit and loss on the respective fractions gives an overall gain of 12 2/3%.

question: A man purchased 50 dozen bananas. Five dozen bananas got spoiled and could not be sold. He sold two-thirds of the remaining bananas at a profit of 20% per dozen and the rest at a profit of 5% per dozen. What was his overall gain/loss percentage?
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति ने 50 दर्जन केले खरीदे। उनमें से 5 दर्जन केले खराब हो गए और बेचे नहीं जा सके। उसने बचे हुए केलों के दो-तिहाई भाग को 20% लाभ पर तथा शेष को 5% लाभ पर बेचा। पूरे लेन-देन में उसका लाभ/हानि प्रतिशत क्या रहा?
explanation: Considering the spoiled bananas and weighted profits on the remaining bananas, the overall result is a gain of 3.5%.

question: A man buys 120 toys at the same cost price. He sells 45% of the toys at 40% profit, one-third of the remaining toys at 20% profit, and the rest at a loss equal to the cost price of 14 toys. What is his overall profit percentage?
questionHindi: एक व्यक्ति 120 खिलौने समान लागत मूल्य पर खरीदता है। वह 45% खिलौनों को 40% लाभ पर, शेष के एक-तिहाई को 20% लाभ पर तथा बाकी को 14 खिलौनों के लागत मूल्य के बराबर हानि पर बेचता है। उसका कुल लाभ प्रतिशत क्या है?
explanation: Calculating total profit from the first two groups and subtracting the loss equivalent to 14 toys gives an overall profit of 8 1/3%.

question: One-third of goods are sold at a 15% profit, 25% of the goods are sold at a 20% profit and the rest at a 20% loss. If the total profit of ₹138.50 is earned on the whole transaction, then the value of the goods is:

The cost of a washing machine is 40% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 18% and that of the TV decreases by 10%, then what is the change in the total cost of 5 washing machines and 2 TVs?
A medical store owner purchased medicines worth ₹18,000. He sold 2/5 part of the medicine at a 35% loss. On what gain should he sell the rest so that he has neither gain nor loss?
explanation: Loss on 2/5 part = 35% × 2/5 = 14%. To balance, gain on 3/5 part = 14%. Required gain = 14 ÷ (3/5) = 23⅓%.

question: A person buys 1596 articles for ₹45,300. He sells 608 articles at 25% profit and 456 articles at 20% loss. At what profit/loss percent should he sell the remaining articles so that he gets neither profit nor loss overall?
explanation: Using average CP per article and balancing profit/loss over all articles, required profit on remaining articles = 11.42%.

question: A shopkeeper bought 120 quintals of wheat. 20% of it was sold at 25% loss. At what percent gain should he sell the rest to gain 25% on the whole transaction?
explanation: 20% sold at 25% loss gives net loss = 5%. To get 25% overall profit, remaining 80% must contribute 30%. Required gain = 30/0.8 = 37.5%.

question: 35% of goods were sold at a profit of 65%, while the remaining were sold at x% loss. If the overall loss is 12%, then what is the value of x (correct to one decimal place)?

A man buys goods for ₹8,000. He sells 30% of those goods at a profit of 12% and 40% of the remaining goods at a profit of 25%. At what profit percentage should he sell the remaining goods to gain 30% in the entire transaction?
explanation: Required total profit = 30%. Profit from first two parts is calculated and remaining profit distributed over remaining 42% goods. Result = 46.2%.

question: A shopkeeper mixes three varieties of tea costing ₹60/kg, ₹80/kg and ₹120/kg in the ratio 5 : 8 : 7. At what price per kg should he sell the mixture to earn a 25% profit?

A vegetable vendor bought 100 kg of potatoes at ₹19/kg and spent ₹100 as cartage. He sold 60 kg at 50% profit, half of the remaining stock at 40% profit and half of the still remaining potatoes at 25% profit. What profit percentage should he aim for on the ultimate remaining potatoes to achieve an overall profit of 42%?
explanation: Total CP = ₹2000. Required profit = ₹840. Profit from first three sales = ₹804. Remaining 10 kg must earn ₹36 profit. Profit% = 36/300 = 12% = 0.12.

question: A person purchases 120 coats and sells 50 coats at a gain of 16% and remaining at a gain of 20%. If he had sold all of them at a uniform profit of 12%, he would have got ₹1520 less. What is the cost price of each coat?
explanation: Extra profit = 50×4% + 70×8% = 7.67 coat-equivalents. 7.6% of total CP = 1520. Solving gives CP per coat = ₹200.

question: A shopkeeper buys a product at ₹150 per kg. 15% of the product was damaged. At what price per kg should he sell the remaining product to earn a profit of 20%?
explanation: Assume 100 kg. CP = ₹15000. Required SP = ₹18000. Sellable quantity = 85 kg. SP/kg = 18000/85 = ₹211 13/17.

question: A shopkeeper bought 40 dozen eggs at ₹1.40 each. 80 eggs were broken in transportation. He sold the remaining eggs at ₹1.60 each. What is his profit or loss percent?

If a shopkeeper sells sugar at ₹44.8 per kg, he makes a 12% profit. Due to water seepage, 1/5 of the sugar is damaged. What should be the selling price per kg of the remaining sugar to earn a 5% profit?
explanation: CP/kg = 44.8/1.12 = ₹40. For 100 kg, CP = ₹4000. Required SP = ₹4200. Remaining quantity = 80 kg. SP/kg = 4200/80 = ₹52.5.

question: A fruit seller buys 480 bananas for ₹1200. Some bananas are rotten and thrown away. He sells the remaining bananas at ₹3.5 each and makes a profit of ₹396. What percentage of bananas were thrown away?
explanation: Required SP = 1200 + 396 = ₹1596. Bananas sold = 1596/3.5 = 456. Thrown away = 480−456 = 24. Percentage = 24/480 ×100 = 5%.

question: The cost of 50 dozens of bananas is ₹2400 and the transport cost per banana is ₹0.25. The selling price is ₹10 for a pair of bananas. What is the profit percentage?

The cost price of a computer is ₹4500 less than the cost price of a TV. The TV is sold at a profit of 10% and the computer is sold for ₹24500. If there is a profit of 20% in the whole transaction, then what is the selling price of the TV?
explanation: Let TV CP = x, Computer CP = x−4500. Total SP = 1.2(2x−4500). Also = 1.1x + 24500. Solving gives x = 23000. TV SP = 1.1×23000 = ₹25300.

question: A shopkeeper bought 20 kg rice at ₹55/kg, 25 kg rice at ₹50/kg and 35 kg rice at ₹60/kg. He spent ₹150 on transportation. He mixed all the rice and sold it at ₹62.56/kg. Find the profit percentage.
A vendor buys 20 laptop bags for ₹13,000 and sells them at 15 for ₹10,125. How many laptop bags should be bought and sold to earn a profit of ₹3,225?
explanation: CP per bag = 13000/20 = ₹650. SP per bag = 10125/15 = ₹675. Profit per bag = ₹25. Required bags = 3225/25 = 129. However, answer marked in sheet is 120.

question: Manjeet bought a second-hand motorbike for ₹22,000 and spent ₹3,000 on its overhauling and maintenance. He then sold it with 12% profit. If he had sold it for ₹500 less, then what would have been his profit percentage?
explanation: Total CP = ₹25,000. SP at 12% profit = ₹28,000. If sold for ₹500 less, SP = ₹27,500. Profit = ₹2,500. Profit% = 2500/25000 × 100 = 10%.

question: Ayush buys an old digital camera for ₹9,200 and spends ₹1,200 on its repair. If Ayush sells the digital camera for ₹12,000, what is his profit percentage (correct up to two decimal places)?
A retailer buys 12 pairs of shoes for ₹22,400. His overhead expenses are ₹1,600. If he earns ₹28,500 from the sale of these 12 pairs of shoes, determine his profit percentage.
Arun buys an old car for ₹4,75,000 and spends ₹80,000 on its repairs. If he sells the car for ₹5,85,000, find his gain percentage (rounded up to two decimal places).

A shopkeeper purchased an article for ₹7,200 and spent 9% of its cost on repairs. He sold it to Rajan for ₹8,100. What was the profit percentage on selling the article? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
explanation: Repair cost = 9% of 7200 = ₹648. Total CP = ₹7848. Profit = 8100 − 7848 = ₹252. Profit% = 252/7848 × 100 = 3.21%. Sheet answer marked: 3.12%.

question: Rajni purchased an LED TV set for ₹22,500 and spent ₹800 on its transportation and ₹1,000 on installation. At what price should she sell it so as to earn an overall profit of 20%?
